planting.note: A tall, substantial cultivar best sited toward the back of a bed where its height has room to show off.

directions: Set rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, moisture-holding soil once the ground has warmed, giving this towering selection plenty of room at the back of a border or along a fence line. Its purple-blushed foliage and vivid bloom spikes reward monthly feeding and consistent moisture through the heat of summer. In zone 7b and warmer it can often ride out winter in the ground under heavy mulch; farther north, lift rhizomes after frost blackens the leaves and store them cool and dry.

planting.note: A mid-height selection in the 'Punch' series of bold-flowered cannas.

directions: Plant rhizomes in full sun in fertile, evenly moist soil after the last frost, and feed regularly to sustain its clear lemon-yellow flower spikes through summer. It belongs to the same 'Punch' line as the orange and red forms already grown widely in American gardens, sharing their sturdy, mid-height habit suited to mixed borders and large containers. Where winters dip below the mid-20s, lift and store rhizomes once foliage is killed by frost.

planting.note: A large, vigorous cultivar; give it room rather than crowding it among shorter cannas.

directions: Set rhizomes several inches deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once frost danger has passed, and keep the soil consistently moist through summer to support its large stature and broad leaves. This vigorous, tall-growing selection works well as a temporary screen or anchor planting at the rear of a tropical-style bed. In cold climates, dig and store rhizomes indoors over winter after the first hard frost blackens the foliage.

planting.note: A mid-sized cultivar well suited to mixed perennial borders rather than massed tropical beds.

directions: Plant rhizomes in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun after the soil has warmed, and deadhead faded spikes to keep new blooms coming into fall. This mid-sized selection fits comfortably into a mixed perennial border rather than needing a dedicated tropical bed, pairing its blooms with companion perennials at eye level. Feed monthly during the growing season, and in regions with hard winters, lift and store the rhizomes once frost takes the foliage.

planting.note: An exceptionally tall species selection; reserve it for the back of a bed or as a seasonal screen.

directions: Give this species selection generous room and rich, consistently moist soil in full sun, since it can reach eight feet by late summer. Unlike many of the shorter hybrid cannas bred for compact bedding use, this is a straight Canna indica form grown primarily for its height and the narrow striping along its stems and foliage. Use it as a fast-growing seasonal screen or at the back of a tropical border, and lift rhizomes for winter storage anywhere colder than zone 7.
